summaries:
The chapter opens with the devastation of the Red Death, a horrific plague marked by bleeding pores and swift death, which has claimed half the population. Prince Prospero, defiant and eccentric, retreats with a thousand courtiers to his fortified abbey, sealing themselves off from the plague with iron gates and welds, surrounded by luxury, music, and indulgence. Months later, he hosts a masked ball in seven elaborately themed rooms, each colored differently and illuminated by firelight through stained glass windows, culminating in a black chamber with blood-red panes and a massive ebony clock that chimes hourly, halting all merriment. During the midnight chime, a mysterious figure appears dressed as the Red Death itself—shrouded in grave-cloths and drenched in scarlet blood—instilling terror and silence among the revelers. Prince Prospero, enraged by the blasphemy, pursues the figure with a dagger through all seven chambers, but when he confronts it in the black room, the figure reveals no physical form, and the prince collapses dead. One by one, the courtiers die as the Red Death infiltrates the abbey, and with the last breath of the final reveler, the clock stops and darkness claims all.
[Characters: Prince Prospero, the Red Death (as a spectral figure), the courtiers, the musicians, the masqueraders]
